corrections.issue: Adds an inference not in the text ('positioning is a proxy for manager returns'); Niels says the SocGen Trend Indicator has not performed well historically but is useful for estimating how managers are positioned, and its 19.27% month-to-date gain may be a record.
corrections.fix: The SocGen Trend Indicator has had weak historical performance but is useful for inferring CTA positioning; it was up 19.27% month to date (late January 2026), possibly a record, while CTA indices were up about 5-6%.

corrections.issue: The text does not say fast trend worked in 2022; Kaminski says fast was better in Covid (C10) and that fast was hard and slow better the year before 2025.
corrections.fix: The best trend speed changes by year: fast was hard and slow better in 2024, faster was better in Covid, so no speed always wins.

corrections.issue: Wrong meaning: Niels says the biggest differences between managers in 2025 arose in April (Liberation Day), driven by trade frequency (weekly traders who did not 'panic'), not that weekly trading cut differences.
corrections.fix: In 2025 the largest return differences among CTAs arose in April around Liberation Day, partly from trade frequency: managers who adjusted positions only weekly did not react to the V-shaped move.

corrections.issue: Omits Kaminski's point that faster volatility adjustment was painful at Liberation Day; the asymmetric downsize/resize speed idea is Niels's, in the same chunk.
corrections.fix: Faster volatility adjustment hurt at Liberation Day (cutting into a V-shaped move) but, if vol estimates came back down quickly, captured more of the second half of 2025; Niels adds that the speed for cutting risk and for re-adding it need not be the same.

completeness_estimate: 0.92 - first reader was very thorough on mechanisms, numbers and design-choice findings; missed a few caveats (QIS AUM, unofficial data, inflation analogue, non-vol-adjusted returns) and misread two speed/vol statements.
